title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pages 25-42 of this 'troisième mouture'). The data are a set M of 'pieces' with three relations, plus a dense subset Λ ⊂ M.
- X ≤ Y: inclusion of pieces.
- Z ≪ X: a 'relatively compact' / 'way below' type relation.
- Z °≪ X: a refined version. By the corollary on p.40, Y °≪ X' means X' is the smallest element of the set of X'' ≤ X with Y ≪ X''. It plays the role of the 'minimal open neighbourhood / star of Z'.
- X̃ = {X' ∈ M : X' ≤ X}, the down-set of X.
- omb_Λ(X) = {Z ∈ Λ : Z ≪ X}, the 'shadow' of X in Λ, and omb_Λ(X)° = {Z ∈ Λ : Z °≪ X}.

On p.40 Lemma A states: for X, Y with a common upper bound, X ≤ Y ⇔ X ≪ Y ⇔ omb(X) ⊂ omb(Y) ⇔ omb(X)° ⊂ omb(Y) ⇔ omb(X)° ∩ omb(Y) ≠ ∅.

Grothendieck then introduces a new primitive relation X ≬ Y. It is reflexive, symmetric and stable under passing to smaller pieces (axiom MΛ1/MΛ4, recalled in the margin here). It is a 'compatibility' or 'coherence' relation that replaces the hypothesis 'X and Y have a common upper bound'.

On this page:
1. A crossed-out NB records that the previous reasoning used ≬ only through the derived relation ∥ (X ∥ Y iff not X ≬ Y and X̃ ∩ Ỹ = ∅), and in fact only through ∥ between elements of Λ.
2. Lemma A' asserts that Lemma A remains valid assuming only X ≬ Y.
3. The argument of p.30 needs the identity omb_Λ(X) ∩ omb_Λ(Y) = ⋃_{Z ∈ X̃ ∩ Ỹ} omb_Λ(Z), i.e. the shadow of the 'intersection' is covered by shadows of common sub-pieces. This motivates a new axiom MΛ5: if X ≬ Y and Z ≪ X, Z ≪ Y, then there is Z' ≤ X, Y with Z ≪ Z'. A margin note says one may restrict to Z ∈ Λ. Grothendieck flags this as a genuinely restrictive condition on compatible pairs.
4. Lemma B (margin: 'Lemme 6 p.32', cf. atlas axiom At_M 4 b): if Z °≪ X, Z °≪ Y and X ≬ Y, then X = Y. So compatible 'minimal stars' of the same piece coincide.
5. More generally (Cor.): if X ≬ Y, Z °≪ X and Z ≪ Y, then X ≤ Y. Proof: by density (MΛ2) choose Z0 ∈ Λ with Z0 °≪ Z. Then Z0 °≪ X, so Z0 ∈ omb(X)°, and Z0 ≪ Y, so Z0 ∈ omb(Y). Hence omb(X)° ∩ omb(Y) ≠ ∅, and Lemma A' gives X ≤ Y. Lemma B follows from the corollary by symmetry plus antisymmetry.

Purpose: to axiomatize a 'shadow' structure (M, ≤, ≪, ≬, Λ). Such a structure should come from a topological / tame space presented by an atlas-like family of pieces with a dense family of small pieces. The next page lists the full characteristic axioms MΛ0-MΛ5 and notes that only MΛ4 and MΛ5 involve ≬.
errors: The corollary's proof uses transitivity Z0 °≪ Z °≪ X ⇒ Z0 °≪ X. With °≪ defined via minimality (p.40 corollary), this is not obvious and is not justified on this page; it presumably rests on an earlier lemma (or on Lemma C / the corollary of p.40 together with MΛ1).

Lemma A' is only asserted ('comme lemme A'), not proved. Grothendieck himself notes that it needs the extra axiom MΛ5 to get the intersection-of-shadows formula used on p.30. So A' is conditional on MΛ5.
Lemma A(iv) as transcribed on p.40 ('omb(X°)') should read omb_Λ(X)°, consistent with its use here.

ideas.what: Replacing 'existence of a common upper bound' by an abstract reflexive, symmetric, downward-closed compatibility relation ≬ on the poset of pieces
ideas.modern_name: consistency/coherence predicate (Scott information systems; coherence spaces)
ideas.usually_credited_to: D. Scott (information systems, 1982); J.-Y. Girard (coherence spaces, 1987)

ideas.what: Axiom MΛ5: for compatible X, Y, the shadow of the 'intersection' is the union of shadows of common sub-pieces (interpolation of ≪ below two compatible pieces)
ideas.modern_name: local intersection / interpolation axiom for a way-below relation on a basis (continuous posets, formal topology covers)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Scott; Gierz-Hofmann-Keimel-Lawson-Mislove-Scott, Compendium of Continuous Lattices (1980); Sambin, formal topology (1987)

ideas.what: Uniqueness of compatible minimal 'stars': Z °≪ X, Z °≪ Y, X ≬ Y ⇒ X = Y, and the corollary X ≤ Y
ideas.modern_name: uniqueness of minimal (open-star) neighbourhoods in a stratified/cellular atlas

ideas.what: Shadow omb_Λ(X) of a piece in a dense subfamily Λ, used to reconstruct the order
ideas.modern_name: way-below set ↡x restricted to a basis; spatial reconstruction from a basis
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) only announces 'topologie modérée' in general terms

missed.claim: In 1986 Grothendieck independently sets up an axiomatics closely parallel to continuous domains / Scott information systems. It consists of a poset with a way-below-like relation ≪, a dense basis Λ, interpolation axioms, and a primitive consistency relation ≬ replacing boundedness. The aim is analysis situs (reconstructing spaces from atlases of pieces), not semantics. This parallel between his tame-topology foundations and domain theory / formal topology is not noted in the literature.
missed.quote: MA 5 Si X ≬ Y, et si Z ≪ X, Z ≪ Y, alors ∃ Z' ∈ X̃ ∩ Ỹ avec Z ≪ Z'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could link Grothendieck's unpublished 'Analysis situs' programme to pointfree topology and domain theory. It suggests his intended reconstruction of tame spaces from pieces may be read as a representation theorem for (possibly non-Hausdorff) continuous posets with a coherence relation.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine lemmas within an evolving axiomatic system. The mildly notable point is the abstract compatibility relation and interpolation axiom, which parallel domain theory independently, but this is a working draft step rather than a finished result.
transcription_corrections: The relation symbol is the 'between'-like ≬ (compatibility), as on pp.40 and 42, not ⊥̸ / 'not perp'.
The axioms are labelled MΛ (M-Lambda), e.g. margin 'MΛ1' and 'MΛ5'; the '5' is overwritten rather than simply deleted.
'Lemme B' has its letter struck/overwritten in the image (renumbering); the margin reads 'Lemme 6 p.32'.
In the proof, 'Z0 ∈ omb_Λ(X)°' is written with the ° as a superscript on omb_Λ(X).
